classification.habitat: Moist disturbed soils and cultivated areas
classification.distribution: Common in tropical and subtropical India

identification.description: Small herb with pinnate-looking branchlets bearing tiny leaves and small fruits beneath the branchlets.
identification.leaf: Small, simple, alternate on branchlets and arranged in two rows.
identification.fruit: Small globose capsules, characteristically borne below the branchlets.

classical_reference.shloka_reference_status: source-hub-added; exact verse/edition requires text-level verification
reference_hubs: TDU Indian Medicinal Plants Database — Shlokas

modern_information.evidence_summary: Phyllanthus species have been investigated extensively for hepatobiliary and antiviral-related pharmacology; species identification is important.
modern_information.safety_notes: Do not equate preclinical evidence with established clinical efficacy.

exam_points: Fruit position is an important identification feature
viva_questions: How do you distinguish Bhumyamalaki in the field?
student.quick_revision: Bhūmyāmalakī: whole plant; sheeta; traditionally pittahara.

practical_points: Observe underside of branchlets for fruits

doctor.quick_reference: Whole plant is traditionally used; species authentication is important.
